title.zh: 卷一百五十一 列傳第一百〇一: 高崇文 伊慎 朱忠亮 劉昌裔 范希朝 王鍔 閻巨源 孟元陽 趙昌
title.en: Volume 151 Biographies 101: Gao Congwen, Yi Shen, Zhu Zhongliang, Liu Changyi, Fan Xichao, Wan Ge, Yan Juyuan, Meng Yuanyang, Zhao Chang
title.raw: 卷一百五十一 列傳第一百〇一: 高崇文 伊慎 朱忠亮 劉昌裔 范希朝 王鍔 閻巨源 孟元陽 趙昌 Volume 151 Biographies 101: Gao Congwen, Yi Shen, Zhu Zhongliang, Liu Changyi, Fan Xichao, Wan Ge, Yan Juyuan, Meng Yuanyang, Zhao Chang

meta.sourceNote: Body restored from Wikisource juan 151 to match the ChineseNotes chapter heading. The previous Wikisource import used the file number instead of the traditional juan.

sentences.zh: 高崇文，其先渤海人。

translations.literal: Gao Congwen—his ancestors were people of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Congwen was descended from people of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 崇文生幽州，樸厚寡言，少從平盧軍。

translations.literal: Congwen was born in Youzhou; plain, solid, and sparing of words; in youth he joined the Pinglu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Congwen was born in Youzhou. Plain and solid, sparing of speech, in his youth he entered the Pinglu Army.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，隨韓全義鎮長武城，治軍有聲。

translations.literal: During the Zhenyuan era, he followed Han Quanyi in garrisoning Changwu Fortress; his administration of the army won renown.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenyuan era he followed Han Quanyi in garrisoning Changwu Fortress, and his command of the army won renown.

sentences.zh: 五年夏，吐蕃三萬寇寧州，崇文率甲士三千救之，戰於佛堂原，大破之，死者過半。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, summer, thirty thousand Tibetans raided Ning Prefecture; Congwen led three thousand armored soldiers to the rescue, fought at Fotang Plain, routed them thoroughly, and more than half the enemy died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, summer, thirty thousand Tibetans raided Ning Prefecture. Congwen led three thousand armored soldiers to the rescue, fought at Fotang Plain, and routed them; more than half the enemy were killed.

sentences.zh: 韓全義入覲，崇文掌行營節度留務，遷兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: When Han Quanyi entered court for an audience, Congwen handled the affairs left behind by the mobile headquarters and provisional commissioner of the circuit; he was transferred and additionally made Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Quanyi went to court for an audience, Congwen managed the mobile headquarters and provisional affairs of the circuit and was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief as well.

sentences.zh: 十四年，為長武城使，積粟練兵，軍聲大振。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he became commissioner of Changwu Fortress; he accumulated grain and drilled troops, and the army's reputation greatly stirred.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he became commissioner of Changwu Fortress. He stockpiled grain and drilled troops, and the army's reputation rose sharply.

sentences.zh: 永貞元年冬，劉辟阻兵，朝議討伐，宰臣杜黃裳以為獨任崇文，可以成功。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Yongzhen, Liu Pi obstructed the military; the court discussed a punitive campaign, and Grand Councillor Du Huangshang held that entrusting Congwen alone could succeed.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of Yongzhen, Liu Pi raised arms in defiance. The court debated a punitive campaign, and Grand Councillor Du Huangshang argued that entrusting Congwen alone would succeed.

sentences.zh: 元和元年春，拜檢校工部尚書、兼御史大夫，充左神策行營節度使，兼統左右神策、奉天麟遊諸鎮兵以討辟。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Yuanhe, he was appointed Acting Minister of Works, concurrently Grand Censor, and Mobile Headquarters Commissioner of the Left Shence Army, additionally commanding the Left and Right Shence, Fengtian, and Linyou garrisons to campaign against Pi.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first year of Yuanhe he was appointed Acting Minister of Works and Grand Censor, made Mobile Headquarters Commissioner of the Left Shence Army, and given command of the Left and Right Shence, Fengtian, and Linyou garrisons to campaign against Pi.

sentences.zh: 時宿將專征者甚眾，人人自謂當選，及詔出大驚。

translations.literal: At the time many veteran generals who held independent commands each fancied he would be chosen; when the edict issued, all were greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Many veteran generals who held independent commands each believed he would be chosen. When the edict appeared, all were greatly astonished.

sentences.zh: 崇文在長武城，練卒五千，常若寇至。

translations.literal: Congwen was at Changwu Fortress, drilling five thousand troops, always as if an enemy were at hand.
translations.idiomatic: At Changwu Fortress Congwen drilled five thousand troops, always as though an enemy were at hand.

sentences.zh: 及是，中使至長武，卯時宣命，而辰時出師五千，器用無闕者。

translations.literal: At this time, when the court envoy reached Changwu at the mao hour to proclaim the command, by the chen hour five thousand troops had marched out, none lacking in arms or equipment.
translations.idiomatic: When the court envoy reached Changwu at the mao hour to proclaim the command, by the chen hour five thousand troops had marched out with no lack of arms or equipment.

sentences.zh: 軍至興元，軍中有折逆旅之匕箸，斬之以徇。

translations.literal: When the army reached Xingyuan, in the ranks someone broke the inn's spoons and chopsticks; he had the man beheaded as an example.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Xingyuan, a soldier broke an inn's spoons and chopsticks. Congwen had him beheaded as a warning.

sentences.zh: 西從閬中入，遂卻劍門之師，解梓潼之圍，賊將邢泚遁歸。

translations.literal: Marching west through Langzhong, he then repelled the army at Jianmen, lifted the siege of Zitong, and the rebel general Xing Ci fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Marching west through Langzhong, he repelled the army at Jianmen, lifted the siege of Zitong, and the rebel general Xing Ci fled back.

sentences.zh: 屯軍梓州，因拜崇文為東川節度使。

translations.literal: He encamped at Zizhou, and Congwen was thereupon appointed Military Commissioner of Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He encamped at Zizhou, and Congwen was thereupon appointed Military Commissioner of Dongchuan.

sentences.zh: 先是，劉辟攻陷東川，擒節度使李康；

translations.literal: Earlier, Liu Pi had attacked and taken Dongchuan and captured the Military Commissioner Li Kang;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu Pi had attacked and taken Dongchuan and captured the Military Commissioner Li Kang;

sentences.zh: 及崇文克梓州，乃歸康求雪己罪，崇文以康敗軍失守，遂斬之。

translations.literal: When Congwen took Zizhou, Li Kang was sent back to plead that his own crimes be cleared; Congwen, on the grounds that Kang had lost his army and abandoned his post, had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Congwen took Zizhou, Li Kang was sent back to plead that his own crimes be cleared. Congwen, holding that Kang had lost his army and abandoned his post, had him executed.

sentences.zh: 成都北一百五十里有鹿頭山，扼兩川之要，辟築城以守，又連八柵，張掎角之勢以拒王師。

translations.literal: One hundred fifty li north of Chengdu stood Mount Lutou, commanding the vital pass between the two river circuits; Pi built a fortress to hold it and linked eight stockades, spreading a pincer formation to resist the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred fifty li north of Chengdu stood Mount Lutou, commanding the vital pass between the two river circuits. Pi built a fortress to hold it and linked eight stockades in a pincer formation to resist the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 是日，破賊二萬於鹿頭城下，大雨如註，不克登，乃止。

translations.literal: That day, he broke twenty thousand rebels beneath Lutou City; rain poured like a torrent, and unable to mount the assault, he halted.
translations.idiomatic: That day he broke twenty thousand rebels beneath Lutou City. Rain poured down in torrents; unable to storm the heights, he halted.

sentences.zh: 明日，又破於萬勝堆。

translations.literal: The next day, he broke them again at Wansheng Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he broke them again at Wansheng Ridge.

sentences.zh: 堆在鹿頭之東，使驍將高霞寓親鼓，士扳緣而上，矢石如雨；

translations.literal: The ridge lay east of Lutou; he sent the fierce general Gao Xiayu to beat the drums in person, and soldiers climbed hand over hand; arrows and stones fell like rain;
translations.idiomatic: The ridge lay east of Lutou. He sent the fierce general Gao Xiayu to beat the drums in person, and soldiers climbed hand over hand while arrows and stones fell like rain;

sentences.zh: 又命敢死士連登，奪其堆，燒其柵，柵中之賊殲焉。

translations.literal: He also ordered dare-to-die men to climb in succession, seized the ridge, burned the stockades, and the rebels within the stockades were annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered dare-to-die men to climb in succession, seized the ridge, burned the stockades, and annihilated the rebels within them.

sentences.zh: 遂據堆下瞰鹿頭城，城中人物可數。

translations.literal: He then held the ridge overlooking Lutou City; the people and objects in the city could be counted.
translations.idiomatic: He then held the ridge overlooking Lutou City, where the people and objects below could be counted.

sentences.zh: 凡八大戰皆大捷，賊搖心矣。

translations.literal: In all eight great battles, each ended in great victory, and the rebels' hearts trembled.
translations.idiomatic: In eight great battles he won great victories each time, and the rebels' hearts trembled.

sentences.zh: 八月，阿跌光顏與崇文約，到行營愆一日。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Adie Guangyan agreed with Congwen to reach headquarters one day late.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Adie Guangyan had agreed with Congwen to reach headquarters one day late.

sentences.zh: 懼誅，乃深入以自贖，故軍於鹿頭西大河之口，以斷賊糧道，賊大駭。

translations.literal: Fearing punishment, he therefore pushed deep into enemy territory to redeem himself; so his army encamped at the mouth of the great river west of Lutou to cut the rebels' grain route, and the rebels were greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing punishment, he pushed deep into enemy territory to redeem himself. His army encamped at the mouth of the great river west of Lutou to cut the rebels' grain route, and the rebels were greatly terrified.

sentences.zh: 是日，賊綿江柵將李文悅以三千人歸順，尋而鹿頭將仇良輔舉城降者眾二萬。

translations.literal: That day, Pi's palisade commander along the Mian River, Li Wenyue, submitted with three thousand men; soon the Lutou garrison commander Qiu Liangfu surrendered the city with twenty thousand more.
translations.idiomatic: That day Pi's palisade commander along the Mian River, Li Wenyue, submitted with three thousand men. Soon the Lutou garrison commander Qiu Liangfu surrendered the city with twenty thousand more.

sentences.zh: 辟之男方叔、子婿蘇強，先監良輔軍，是日械系送京師，降卒投戈面縛者彌十數里，遂長驅而直指成都。

translations.literal: Pi's male relative Fangshu and son-in-law Su Qiang had earlier overseen Liangfu's army; that day they were shackled and sent to the capital; surrendered troops cast aside weapons and came bound face-forward for more than ten li, then the army drove straight toward Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Pi's male relative Fangshu and son-in-law Su Qiang had earlier overseen Liangfu's army. That day they were shackled and sent to the capital. Surrendered troops cast aside weapons and came bound face-forward for more than ten li, and the army drove straight toward Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 德陽等縣城皆鎮以重兵，莫不望旗率服，師無留行。

translations.literal: The county towns such as Deyang were all garrisoned with heavy troops; none failed to lower their banners and submit at once; the army marched without delay.
translations.idiomatic: County towns such as Deyang were all garrisoned with heavy troops, yet none failed to lower their banners and submit at once. The army marched without delay.

sentences.zh: 辟大懼，以親兵及逆黨盧文若賫重寶西走吐蕃。

translations.literal: Pi was greatly afraid; with his personal guard and the traitor Lu Wenruo he fled west bearing heavy treasures toward Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Pi was greatly afraid. With his personal guard and the traitor Lu Wenruo he fled west bearing heavy treasures toward Tibet.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃素受其賂，且將啟之。

translations.literal: Tibet had long accepted his bribes and was about to open the way for him.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet had long accepted his bribes and was about to open the way for him.

sentences.zh: 崇文遣高霞寓、酈定進倍道追之，至羊灌田及焉。

translations.literal: Congwen sent Gao Xiayu and Li Dingjin by forced march in pursuit; at Yangguantian they overtook them.
translations.idiomatic: Congwen sent Gao Xiayu and Li Dingjin by forced march in pursuit and overtook them at Yangguantian.

sentences.zh: 辟自投岷江，擒於湧湍之中。

translations.literal: Pi threw himself into the Min River and was captured in the rushing current.
translations.idiomatic: Pi threw himself into the Min River and was captured in the rushing current.

sentences.zh: 西蜀平，乃檻辟送京師伏法。

translations.literal: With western Shu pacified, Pi was placed in a caged cart and sent to the capital to suffer the penalty of law.
translations.idiomatic: With western Shu pacified, Pi was placed in a caged cart and sent to the capital to suffer the penalty of law.

sentences.zh: 文若赴水死。

translations.literal: Wenruo threw himself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Wenruo threw himself into the water and died.

sentences.zh: 王師入成都，介士屯於大逵，軍令嚴肅，珍寶山積，市井不移，無秋毫之犯。

translations.literal: When the imperial army entered Chengdu, armored men encamped in the great thoroughfare; military discipline was stern, treasures piled like hills, the markets unmoved— not the slightest infraction.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army entered Chengdu, armored men encamped in the great thoroughfare. Military discipline was stern; treasures piled like hills and the markets were unmoved—not the slightest infraction.

sentences.zh: 先是，賊將邢泚以兵二萬為鹿頭之援，既降又貳，斬之以徇。

translations.literal: Earlier, the rebel general Xing Ci, with twenty thousand men as relief for Lutou, had surrendered and then turned traitor again; he was beheaded as an example.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the rebel general Xing Ci, with twenty thousand men as relief for Lutou, had surrendered and then turned traitor again. He was beheaded as a warning.

sentences.zh: 衣冠陷逆者，皆匍匐衙門請命，崇文條奏全活之。

translations.literal: Officials and gentry who had fallen with the rebellion all crawled to the yamen gate to plead for their lives; Congwen memorialized item by item to preserve them all.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and gentry who had fallen with the rebellion all crawled to the yamen gate to plead for their lives. Congwen memorialized item by item to preserve them all.

sentences.zh: 制授崇文檢校司空，兼成都尹，充劍南西川節度、管內度支營田觀察處置、統押近界諸蠻，西山八國雲南安撫等使。

translations.literal: By decree he was appointed Acting Minister of Works, concurrently Prefect of Chengdu, Military Commissioner of the Western Sichuan Circuit of Jiannan, Commissioner for Revenue, Agricultural Colonies, and Observation and Disposition within the circuit, Overseer of the Nearby Frontier Tribes, and Commissioner for Pacification of the Eight Kingdoms of the Western Mountains, Yunnan, and so forth.
translations.idiomatic: By decree he was appointed Acting Minister of Works and Prefect of Chengdu, made Military Commissioner of the Western Sichuan Circuit of Jiannan with authority over revenue, agricultural colonies, observation, and disposition within the circuit, given oversight of the nearby frontier tribes, and made Commissioner for Pacification of the Eight Kingdoms of the Western Mountains, Yunnan, and so forth.

sentences.zh: 改封南平郡王，食實封三百戶，詔刻石紀功於鹿頭山下。

translations.literal: His fief was changed to Duke of Nanping, with three hundred households of actual fief; an edict ordered a stone carved at the foot of Mount Lutou to record his merit.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was changed to Duke of Nanping with three hundred households of actual fief. An edict ordered a stone carved at the foot of Mount Lutou to record his merit.

sentences.zh: 崇文不通文字，厭大府案牘諮稟之繁，且以優富之地，無所陳力，乞居塞上以扞邊戍，懇疏累上。

translations.literal: Congwen did not know writing; he was wearied by the vast paperwork and consultative reports of the great prefecture, and because it was a richly favored land where he had no way to show his strength, he repeatedly submitted earnest memorials asking to reside on the frontier to defend the border garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Congwen did not know writing and was wearied by the vast paperwork and consultative reports of the great prefecture. Because it was a richly favored land where he had no way to show his strength, he repeatedly submitted earnest memorials asking to reside on the frontier to defend the border garrisons.

sentences.zh: 二年冬，制加同中書門下平章事、邠州刺史、邠寧慶三州節度觀察等使，仍充京西都統。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year, by decree he was additionally made Co-equal with the Secretariat, Prefect of Bin Prefecture, Military Commissioner and Observer of the three prefectures of Bin, Ning, and Qing, still serving as overall commander of the western capital region.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year, by decree he was additionally made Co-equal with the Secretariat, Prefect of Bin Prefecture, and Military Commissioner and Observer of the three prefectures of Bin, Ning, and Qing, still serving as overall commander of the western capital region.

sentences.zh: 恃其功而侈心大作，帑藏之富，百工之巧，舉而自隨，蜀都一罄。

translations.literal: Relying on his merit, extravagant ambition swelled greatly; the wealth of the treasuries, the skill of artisans and craftsmen — all he took with himself, and the capital of Shu was emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on his merit, extravagant ambition swelled greatly. The wealth of the treasuries and the skill of artisans and craftsmen—all he took with himself, and the capital of Shu was emptied.

sentences.zh: 以不習朝儀，憚於入覲，優詔令便道之鎮。

translations.literal: Because he was unskilled in court ritual, he dreaded entering for an audience; a gracious edict permitted him to proceed directly to his command by convenient route.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was unskilled in court ritual, he dreaded entering for an audience. A gracious edict permitted him to proceed directly to his command by convenient route.

sentences.zh: 居三年，大修戎備。

translations.literal: After three years in office, he greatly restored military preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in office he greatly restored military preparedness.

sentences.zh: 元和四年卒，年六十四，廢朝三日，贈司徒，謚曰威武，配享憲宗廟庭。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanhe he died, age sixty-four; court mourning was suspended for three days; he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor; posthumous title Wei Wu; enshrined in Emperor Xianzong's temple courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanhe he died at the age of sixty-four. Court mourning was suspended for three days. He was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, given the posthumous title Wei Wu, and enshrined in Emperor Xianzong's temple courtyard.

sentences.zh: 子承簡，少為忠武軍部將，後入神策軍。

translations.literal: His son Chengjian, in youth a staff officer of the Zhongwu Army, later entered the Shence Army.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chengjian, in youth a staff officer of the Zhongwu Army, later entered the Shence Army.

sentences.zh: 以父征劉辟，拜嘉王傅。

translations.literal: Because his father campaigned against Liu Pi, he was appointed Tutor to the Prince of Jia.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father campaigned against Liu Pi, he was appointed Tutor to the Prince of Jia.

sentences.zh: 裴度征淮、蔡，奏承簡以本官兼御史中丞，為其軍都押衙。

translations.literal: When Pei Du campaigned against Huai and Cai, he memorialized Chengjian to serve as Vice Censor-in-Chief in his original office and as chief adjutant of his army.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Du campaigned against Huai and Cai, he memorialized Chengjian to serve as Vice Censor-in-Chief in his original office and as chief adjutant of his army.

sentences.zh: 淮西平，詔以郾城、上蔡、遂平三縣為溵州，治郾城，用承簡為刺史。

translations.literal: When Huai and Cai were pacified, an edict made the three counties of Yancheng, Shangcai, and Suiping into a new Wen Prefecture, with its seat at Yancheng; Chengjian was appointed its prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai and Cai were pacified, an edict made the three counties of Yancheng, Shangcai, and Suiping into the new Wen Prefecture, with its seat at Yancheng, and appointed Chengjian its prefect.

sentences.zh: 尋轉邢州刺史，值觀察使責時賦急，承簡代數百戶出其租。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to Prefect of Xing Prefecture; when the observer urgently exacted seasonal levies, Chengjian paid the rent for several hundred households on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Prefect of Xing Prefecture. When the observer urgently exacted seasonal levies, Chengjian paid the rent for several hundred households on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 遷宋州刺史，屬汴州逐其帥，以部將李絺行帥事。

translations.literal: Transferred to Prefect of Song Prefecture; when Bian Prefecture drove out its commander, the staff officer Li Chi acted as commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Prefect of Song Prefecture. When Bian Prefecture drove out its commander, the staff officer Li Chi acted as commander.

sentences.zh: 絺遣其將責宋官私財物，承簡執而囚之。

translations.literal: Chi sent his officer to exact private goods from Song officials; Chengjian seized and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Chi sent his officer to exact private goods from Song officials. Chengjian seized and imprisoned him.

sentences.zh: 自是汴使來者，輒系之，一日並出斬於軍門之外，威震郡中。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever Bian envoys came, he bound them; one day he had them all beheaded outside the army gate, and awe filled the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, whenever Bian envoys came, he bound them. One day he had them all beheaded outside the army gate, and awe filled the commandery.

sentences.zh: 及絺兵大至，宋州凡三城，已陷南一城，承簡保北兩城以拒，凡十餘戰。

translations.literal: When Chi's army arrived in force, Song Prefecture had three walled cities; the southern city had already fallen, and Chengjian held the northern two cities to resist, fighting more than ten battles in all.
translations.idiomatic: When Chi's army arrived in force, Song Prefecture had three walled cities. The southern city had already fallen, and Chengjian held the northern two cities to resist, fighting more than ten battles in all.

sentences.zh: 會徐州救兵至，絺為汴將李質執之，傳送京師，兵圍宋者即遁去。

translations.literal: When Xuzhou relief troops arrived, Chi was seized by the Bian officer Li Zhi and sent to the capital; the army besieging Song at once dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuzhou relief troops arrived, Chi was seized by the Bian officer Li Zhi and sent to the capital, and the army besieging Song at once dispersed.

sentences.zh: 授承簡檢校左散騎常侍、充海沂密等州節度觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: Chengjian was appointed Acting Left Regular Attendant and Cavalier and made Military Commissioner and Observer of Hai, Yi, Mi, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Chengjian was appointed Acting Left Regular Attendant and Cavalier and made Military Commissioner and Observer of Hai, Yi, Mi, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 俄遷檢校工部尚書、義成軍節度、鄭滑潁等州觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Acting Minister of Works, Military Commissioner of the Yicheng Army, and Observer of Zheng, Hua, Ying, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Acting Minister of Works, Military Commissioner of the Yicheng Army, and Observer of Zheng, Hua, Ying, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 就加檢校尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was thereupon additionally made Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon additionally made Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 入拜右金吾衛大將軍，充右街使。

translations.literal: He entered court as Grand General of the Right Jinwu Guard and served as commander of the Right Street.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Grand General of the Right Jinwu Guard and served as commander of the Right Street.

sentences.zh: 復出為邠寧慶等州節度觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: He went out again as Military Commissioner and Observer of Bin, Ning, Qing, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He went out again as Military Commissioner and Observer of Bin, Ning, Qing, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 先是，羌虜多以秋月犯西邊，承簡請軍寧州以備之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qiang and Rong tribesmen often raided the western border in the autumn moon; Chengjian requested an army at Ning Prefecture to guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Qiang and Rong tribesmen often raided the western border in the autumn months. Chengjian requested an army at Ning Prefecture to guard against them.

sentences.zh: 因疾，上言乞入覲，即隨表詣闕。

translations.literal: Because of illness, he submitted a memorial asking to enter for an audience and at once followed his memorial to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Because of illness he submitted a memorial asking to enter for an audience and at once followed his memorial to the capital.

sentences.zh: 太和元年八月，行至永壽縣傳舍卒，贈司空。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Taihe, he died at the relay station in Yongshou County; he was posthumously granted Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of Taihe he died at the relay station in Yongshou County and was posthumously granted Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 崇文孫駢，歷位崇顯，終淮南節度使，自有傳。

translations.literal: Congwen's grandson Pian held posts of lofty rank and ended as Military Commissioner of Huainan; he has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Congwen's grandson Pian held posts of lofty rank and ended as Military Commissioner of Huainan; he has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 伊慎，兗州人。

translations.literal: Yi Shen was a man of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Shen was a man of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 善騎射，始為果毅。

translations.literal: Skilled in mounted archery, he began as a guoyi officer.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in mounted archery, he began as a guoyi officer.

sentences.zh: 喪母，將營合祔，不識其父之墓。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he was about to prepare joint burial, but did not know his father's grave.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he was about to prepare joint burial but did not know his father's grave.

sentences.zh: 晝夜號哭，未浹日，夢寐有指導焉。

translations.literal: Day and night he wailed; before a full day had passed, in sleep and dream there was guidance.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night he wailed. Before a full day had passed, in sleep and dream there was guidance.

sentences.zh: 遂發壟，果得舊記驗。

translations.literal: He then opened the mound and indeed found the old record verified.
translations.idiomatic: He then opened the mound and indeed found the old record verified.

sentences.zh: 大曆八年，江西節度使路嗣恭討嶺南哥舒晃之亂，以慎為先鋒，直逼賊壘，疾戰破之，斬首三千級，由是復始興之地。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dali, when the Jiangxi Military Commissioner Lu Sicong campaigned against the disorder of Geshu Huang in Lingnan, he made Shen the vanguard; he pressed straight to the rebel camp, fought fiercely and broke them, beheaded three thousand, and thereby recovered the lands of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Dali, when the Jiangxi Military Commissioner Lu Sicong campaigned against the disorder of Geshu Huang in Lingnan, he made Shen the vanguard. Shen pressed straight to the rebel camp, fought fiercely and broke them, beheaded three thousand, and thereby recovered the lands of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 未幾，與諸將追斬晃於泔溪，函首獻於闕下。

translations.literal: Before long, with the other generals he pursued and beheaded Huang at Gan Stream and sent the head in a box to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, with the other generals he pursued and beheaded Huang at Gan Stream and sent the head in a box to the capital.

sentences.zh: 嗣恭表慎功，授連州長史，知當州團練副使，三遷江州別駕。

translations.literal: Sicong memorialized Shen's merit; he was appointed Chief of Lian Prefecture, knowing the Deputy Commissioner of the Prefecture's Militia, and after three promotions became Vice Prefect of Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sicong memorialized Shen's merit. He was appointed Chief of Lian Prefecture and Deputy Commissioner of the Prefecture's Militia, and after three promotions became Vice Prefect of Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 討梁崇義之歲，慎以江西牙將從李希烈，摧鋒陷敵，功又居多。

translations.literal: In the year of the campaign against Liang Chongyi, Shen as a Jiangxi staff officer followed Li Xilie, smashed the vanguard and broke the enemy, and his merit was again foremost.
translations.idiomatic: In the year of the campaign against Liang Chongyi, Shen as a Jiangxi staff officer followed Li Xilie, smashed the vanguard and broke the enemy, and his merit was again foremost.

sentences.zh: 江漢既平，希烈愛慎之材，數遺善馬，意欲縻之，慎以計遁，歸命本道。

translations.literal: When the Jiang and Han regions were pacified, Xilie admired Shen's talent and repeatedly sent fine horses, intending to hold him; Shen escaped by stratagem and returned to report to his own circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiang and Han regions were pacified, Xilie admired Shen's talent and repeatedly sent fine horses, intending to hold him. Shen escaped by stratagem and returned to report to his own circuit.

sentences.zh: 明年，希烈果反。

translations.literal: The next year, Xilie indeed rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Xilie indeed rebelled.

sentences.zh: 嗣曹王臯始至鐘陵，大集將吏，得慎而壯之。

translations.literal: When Prince Cao Wang Gao first reached Zhongling, he greatly gathered officers and clerks and, obtaining Shen, was impressed by him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Cao Wang Gao first reached Zhongling, he greatly gathered officers and clerks and, obtaining Shen, was impressed by him.

sentences.zh: 大集兵將，繕理舟師。

translations.literal: He greatly gathered troops and generals and readied the river fleet.
translations.idiomatic: He greatly gathered troops and generals and readied the river fleet.

sentences.zh: 希烈懼慎為曹王所任，遺慎七屬之甲，詐為慎書行間焉。

translations.literal: Xilie feared that Shen would be entrusted by Prince Cao Wang; he sent Shen seven-layer armor and forged a letter in Shen's name to circulate among the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie feared that Shen would be entrusted by Prince Cao Wang. He sent Shen seven-layer armor and forged a letter in Shen's name to circulate among the ranks.

sentences.zh: 上遣中使即軍以詰之，曹王乃抗疏論雪。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a court envoy to the army to question him; Prince Cao Wang then submitted a memorial in protest to clear him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a court envoy to the army to question him. Prince Cao Wang then submitted a memorial in protest to clear him.

sentences.zh: 上章未報，會賊兵溯江來寇，曹王乃召慎勉之令戰，大破三千餘眾，朝廷始信其不貳。

translations.literal: Before the memorial was answered, rebel troops came upriver to raid; Prince Cao Wang then summoned Shen and urged him to fight, breaking more than three thousand; the court then believed he was not disloyal.
translations.idiomatic: Before the memorial was answered, rebel troops came upriver to raid. Prince Cao Wang then summoned Shen and urged him to fight, and he broke more than three thousand. The court then believed he was not disloyal.

sentences.zh: 累破蔡山柵，取蘄州，降其將李良。

translations.literal: He repeatedly broke the stockade at Mount Cai, took Qizhou, and made the general Li Liang submit.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly broke the stockade at Mount Cai, took Qizhou, and made the general Li Liang submit.

sentences.zh: 又攻黃梅縣，殺賊將韓霜露，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: He also attacked Huangmei County, killed the rebel general Han Shuanglu, and beheaded more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He also attacked Huangmei County, killed the rebel general Han Shuanglu, and beheaded more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 優詔褒異，授試太子詹事，封南充郡王，又兼御史中丞、蘄州刺史，充節度都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: A gracious edict praised him with distinction; he was appointed Acting Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, enfeoffed as Duke of Nanchong, and additionally made Vice Censor-in-Chief and Prefect of Qizhou, serving as Commissioner of the Circuit's Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A gracious edict praised him with distinction. He was appointed Acting Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, enfeoffed as Duke of Nanchong, and additionally made Vice Censor-in-Chief and Prefect of Qizhou, serving as Commissioner of the Circuit's Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 建中末，車駕在梁、洋，鹽鐵使包佶以金幣溯江將進獻，次於蘄口。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jianzhong era, when the imperial carriage was at Liang and Yang, the Salt and Iron Commissioner Bao Ji, with gold and silks, went upriver intending to present tribute and halted at Qikou.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jianzhong era, when the imperial carriage was at Liang and Yang, the Salt and Iron Commissioner Bao Ji, with gold and silks, went upriver intending to present tribute and halted at Qikou.

sentences.zh: 時賊已屠汴州，遣驍將杜少誠將步騎萬餘來寇黃梅，以絕江道。

translations.literal: At the time the rebels had already slaughtered Bian Prefecture; they sent the fierce general Du Shaoqian with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry to raid Huangmei and cut the river route.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the rebels had already slaughtered Bian Prefecture. They sent the fierce general Du Shaoqian with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry to raid Huangmei and cut the river route.

sentences.zh: 慎兵七千，遇於永安戍。

translations.literal: Shen had seven thousand troops and met them at Yong'an Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Shen had seven thousand troops and met them at Yong'an Garrison.

sentences.zh: 慎列樹三柵，相去數里，偃旗臥鼓。

translations.literal: Shen arrayed three stockades in a line, several li apart, lowered banners and silenced drums.
translations.idiomatic: Shen arrayed three stockades in a line, several li apart, lowered banners and silenced drums.

sentences.zh: 於中柵聲鼓，三柵悉兵以擊，賊軍大亂，少誠脫身以免，斬級不可勝數，江路遂通。

translations.literal: At the middle stockade he sounded the drums; all three stockades sent troops to strike, and the rebel army fell into great disorder; Shaoqian escaped by himself, and the slain were beyond counting; the river route was then open.
translations.idiomatic: At the middle stockade he sounded the drums, and all three stockades sent troops to strike. The rebel army fell into great disorder. Shaoqian escaped by himself, and the slain were beyond counting. The river route was then open.

sentences.zh: 又破茍莽柵，進兵圍安州。

translations.literal: He also broke the stockade at Gou Mang and advanced to besiege An Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He also broke the stockade at Gou Mang and advanced to besiege An Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 賊阻涢水，攻之不能下。

translations.literal: The rebels blocked the Ru River; he could not take it by assault.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels blocked the Ru River, and he could not take it by assault.

sentences.zh: 希烈遣其甥劉戒虛將騎八千來援，慎分兵迎擊，戰於應山，擒戒虛，縛示城下，遂開門請罪。

translations.literal: Xilie sent his nephew Liu Jie'xu with eight thousand cavalry to relieve them; Shen divided troops to meet and strike, fought at Yingshan, captured Jie'xu, bound him and displayed him beneath the wall, and the city then opened its gates to plead guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie sent his nephew Liu Jie'xu with eight thousand cavalry to relieve them. Shen divided troops to meet and strike, fought at Yingshan, captured Jie'xu, bound him and displayed him beneath the wall, and the city then opened its gates to plead guilt.

sentences.zh: 以功拜安州刺史、兼御史大夫，仍賜實封一百戶。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed Prefect of An Prefecture and concurrently Grand Censor, still granted one hundred households of actual fief.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was appointed Prefect of An Prefecture and concurrently Grand Censor, and was granted one hundred households of actual fief.

sentences.zh: 希烈又遣將援隋州，慎擊之於厲鄉，走康叔夜，斬首五千級。

translations.literal: Xilie again sent generals to relieve Suizhou; Shen struck them at Li Village, routed Kang Shuye, and beheaded five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie again sent generals to relieve Suizhou. Shen struck them at Li Village, routed Kang Shuye, and beheaded five thousand.

sentences.zh: 希烈死，李惠登為賊守隋州，慎飛書招諭，惠登遂以城降。

translations.literal: When Xilie died, Li Huideng held Suizhou for the rebels; Shen sent a swift letter to summon and instruct him, and Huideng then submitted the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Xilie died, Li Huideng held Suizhou for the rebels. Shen sent a swift letter to summon and instruct him, and Huideng then submitted the city.

sentences.zh: 因密奏惠登可用，詔授隋州刺史。

translations.literal: He then secretly memorialized that Huideng could be employed; an edict appointed Huideng Prefect of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then secretly memorialized that Huideng could be employed, and an edict appointed Huideng Prefect of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 貞元十五年，以慎為安黃等州節度、管內支度營田觀察等使。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan, Shen was made Military Commissioner of An, Huang, and other prefectures, with authority over revenue, agricultural colonies, and observation within the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan, Shen was made Military Commissioner of An, Huang, and other prefectures, with authority over revenue, agricultural colonies, and observation within the circuit.

sentences.zh: 十六年，吳少誠阻命，詔以本道步騎五千，兼統荊南、湖南、江西三道兵，當其一面。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, when Wu Shaocheng defied orders, an edict made five thousand infantry and cavalry of this circuit, additionally commanding the armies of Jingnan, Hunan, and Jiangxi, to face him on one front.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, when Wu Shaocheng defied orders, an edict made five thousand infantry and cavalry of this circuit, additionally commanding the armies of Jingnan, Hunan, and Jiangxi, to face him on one front.

sentences.zh: 於申州城南前後破賊數千，以例加檢校刑部尚書。

translations.literal: South of Shen Prefecture city he repeatedly broke several thousand rebels; by precedent he was additionally made Acting Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: South of Shen Prefecture city he repeatedly broke several thousand rebels, and by precedent he was additionally made Acting Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，於安黃置奉義軍額，以為奉義軍節度使、檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, the designation of the Fengyi Army was established in An and Huang; he became Military Commissioner of the Fengyi Army and Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year the designation of the Fengyi Army was established in An and Huang. He became Military Commissioner of the Fengyi Army and Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，入真拜右僕射。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong took the throne, he entered court and was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs in full.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong took the throne, he entered court and was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs in full.

sentences.zh: 元和二年，轉檢校左僕射，兼右金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhe, he was transferred to Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrently Grand General of the Right Jinwu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanhe he was transferred to Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrently Grand General of the Right Jinwu Guard.

sentences.zh: 以賂第五從直求鎮河中，為從直所奏，貶右衛將軍。

translations.literal: He bribed Diwu Congzhi to seek command of Hezhong; Congzhi memorialized against him, and he was demoted to General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He bribed Diwu Congzhi to seek command of Hezhong. Congzhi memorialized against him, and he was demoted to General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 數月，復為檢校尚書右僕射，兼右衛上將軍。

translations.literal: After several months, he was again made Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrently Senior General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After several months he was again made Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrently Senior General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 元和六年卒，年六十八，贈太子太保。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanhe he died, age sixty-eight; he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yuanhe he died at the age of sixty-eight and was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 朱忠亮，本名士明，沛州浚儀人。

translations.literal: Zhu Zhongliang, original name Shiming, was a man of Junyi in Pei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zhongliang, whose original name was Shiming, was a man of Junyi in Pei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初事薛嵩為將。

translations.literal: At first he served Xue Song as a general.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served Xue Song as a general.

sentences.zh: 大曆中，詔鎮普潤縣，掌屯田。

translations.literal: In the Dali era, by edict he garrisoned Puyan County and managed agricultural colonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali era, by edict he garrisoned Puyan County and managed agricultural colonies.

sentences.zh: 朱泚之亂，以麾下四十騎奔奉天。

translations.literal: In Zhu Ci's rebellion, with forty horsemen under his command he fled to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhu Ci's rebellion, with forty horsemen under his command he fled to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 德宗嘉之，封東陽郡王，為「奉天定難功臣」。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong commended him, enfeoffed him as Duke of Dongyang, and made him a "Meritorious Minister Who Settled the Difficulty at Fengtian."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong commended him, enfeoffed him as Duke of Dongyang, and made him a "Meritorious Minister Who Settled the Difficulty at Fengtian."

sentences.zh: 及大駕南幸，為虜騎所獲，系於長安。

translations.literal: When the Great Carriage went south on a progress, he was captured by enemy cavalry and held in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When the Great Carriage went south on a progress, he was captured by enemy cavalry and held in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 賊平，李晟釋之，薦於渾瑊，署定平鎮都虞候。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, Li Sheng released him and recommended him to Hun Zhen, who appointed him Chief Commandant of Dingping Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were pacified, Li Sheng released him and recommended him to Hun Zhen, who appointed him Chief Commandant of Dingping Garrison.

sentences.zh: 鎮使李朝采卒，遂代之。

translations.literal: When the garrison commander Li Chaocai died, he then replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: When the garrison commander Li Chaocai died, he then replaced him.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，加御史大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong took the throne, he was additionally made Grand Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong took the throne, he was additionally made Grand Censor.

sentences.zh: 築臨涇城有勞，特加檢校工部尚書、涇原四鎮節度使，仍賜名。

translations.literal: For merit in building Linyuan Fortress he was specially additionally made Acting Minister of Works and Military Commissioner of the Four Garrisons of Jingyuan, and was still granted his new name.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in building Linyuan Fortress he was specially additionally made Acting Minister of Works and Military Commissioner of the Four Garrisons of Jingyuan, and was still granted his new name.

sentences.zh: 涇土舊俗多賣子，忠亮以俸錢贖而還其親者約二百人。

translations.literal: The custom of the Jing region had long been to sell children; Zhongliang used his salary to redeem and return to their kin about two hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: The custom of the Jing region had long been to sell children. Zhongliang used his salary to redeem and return to their kin about two hundred persons.

sentences.zh: 元和八年卒，贈右僕射。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanhe he died and was posthumously granted Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yuanhe he died and was posthumously granted Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 劉昌裔，太原陽曲人。

translations.literal: Liu Changyi was a man of Yangqu in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Changyi was a man of Yangqu in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 少遊三蜀。

translations.literal: In youth he traveled the Three Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he traveled the Three Shu.

sentences.zh: 楊琳之亂，昌裔說其歸順。

translations.literal: In Yang Lin's rebellion, Changyi persuaded him to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In Yang Lin's rebellion, Changyi persuaded him to submit.

sentences.zh: 及琳授洺州刺史，以昌裔為從事，琳死乃去。

translations.literal: When Lin was appointed Prefect of Luozhou, he made Changyi his staff officer; when Lin died he then left.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin was appointed Prefect of Luozhou, he made Changyi his staff officer. When Lin died he then left.

sentences.zh: 曲環將幽隴兵收濮州也，辟為判官。

translations.literal: When Qu Huan led the You and Long troops to recover Pu Prefecture, he recruited Changyi as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Qu Huan led the You and Long troops to recover Pu Prefecture, he recruited Changyi as administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 詔授監察御史，累加至檢校兵部尚書，賜紫，兼中丞，充營田副使。

translations.literal: By edict he was appointed Investigating Censor; he was repeatedly promoted to Acting Minister of War, granted purple robes, additionally made Vice Censor-in-Chief, and served as Deputy Commissioner of Agricultural Colonies.
translations.idiomatic: By edict he was appointed Investigating Censor. He was repeatedly promoted to Acting Minister of War, granted purple robes, additionally made Vice Censor-in-Chief, and served as Deputy Commissioner of Agricultural Colonies.

sentences.zh: 貞元十五年，環鎮許州，卒，詔上官涚知節度留後。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan, when Huan garrisoned Xu Prefecture and died, an edict made Shangguan Qian provisional commissioner of the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan, when Huan garrisoned Xu Prefecture and died, an edict made Shangguan Qian provisional commissioner of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 吳少誠攻許州，涚領事，欲棄城走。

translations.literal: When Wu Shaocheng attacked Xu Prefecture, Qian took charge of affairs and wished to abandon the city and flee.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Shaocheng attacked Xu Prefecture, Qian took charge of affairs and wished to abandon the city and flee.

sentences.zh: 昌裔追止之曰：「留後既受詔，宜以死守城。

translations.literal: Changyi ran after him and stopped him, saying: "The Acting Commissioner has received an edict — you ought to hold the city and defend it to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Changyi ran after him and stopped him, saying: "The Acting Commissioner has received an edict — you ought to hold the city and defend it to the death.

sentences.zh: 況城中士馬足以破賊，但堅壁不戰，不過五七日，賊勢必衰，我以全制之可也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the men and horses in the city are sufficient to defeat the rebels; if you merely hold the walls and give no battle, in no more than five or seven days the rebels' strength will surely decline, and we can overwhelm them with our full strength."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the men and horses in the city are sufficient to defeat the rebels. If you merely hold the walls and give no battle, in no more than five or seven days the rebels' strength will surely decline, and we can overwhelm them with our full strength."

sentences.zh: 涚然之。

translations.literal: Shangguan Qian approved.
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan Qian agreed.

sentences.zh: 賊日夕攻急，堞壞不得修，昌裔令造戰棚木柵以待；

translations.literal: The rebels pressed the attack day and night; the parapets were ruined and could not be repaired; Changyi ordered battle sheds and wooden palisades built in readiness;
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pressed the attack day and night. The parapets were ruined and could not be repaired. Changyi ordered battle sheds and wooden palisades built in readiness;

sentences.zh: 募壯士破營，得突將千人，鑿城分出，大破之，因立戰棚木柵於城上，城以故不陷。

translations.literal: He recruited stalwart men to break the enemy camp, obtained a thousand shock troops, broke through the wall and sallied forth, and routed them greatly; he then erected battle sheds and wooden palisades on the wall, and the city for that reason did not fall.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited stalwart men to break the enemy camp, obtained a thousand shock troops, broke through the wall and sallied forth, and routed them greatly. He then erected battle sheds and wooden palisades on the wall, and the city for that reason did not fall.

sentences.zh: 兵馬使安國寧與涚不善，謀反以城降賊；

translations.literal: The Horse and Chariot Commissioner An Guoning was on bad terms with Qian and plotted rebellion to surrender the city to the rebels;
translations.idiomatic: The Horse and Chariot Commissioner An Guoning was on bad terms with Qian and plotted rebellion to surrender the city to the rebels;

sentences.zh: 事泄，昌裔密計斬之。

translations.literal: When the affair leaked out, Changyi secretly planned and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair leaked out, Changyi secretly planned and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 即召其麾下千餘人食之，賞縑二匹，伏兵諸要巷，令持縑者悉斬之，無一人得脫。

translations.literal: He then summoned more than a thousand of Guoning's followers and feasted them, rewarding each with two bolts of silk; he hid troops in the key lanes and ordered that all who held silk be beheaded — not one escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned more than a thousand of Guoning's followers and feasted them, rewarding each with two bolts of silk. He hid troops in the key lanes and ordered that all who held silk be beheaded—not one escaped.

sentences.zh: 十六年，以全陳許功，以涚為節度使，昌裔為陳州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, for preserving Chen and Xu, Qian was made Military Commissioner and Changyi Prefect of Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, for preserving Chen and Xu, Qian was made Military Commissioner and Changyi Prefect of Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 韓全義之敗溵水也，與諸道兵皆走保陳州；

translations.literal: When Han Quanyi was defeated at Wen River, he and the armies of the various circuits all fled to hold Chen Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: When Han Quanyi was defeated at Wen River, he and the armies of the various circuits all fled to hold Chen Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 求舍，昌裔登城謂曰：「天子命公討蔡州，今來陳州，義不敢納，請舍城外。」

translations.literal: Seeking lodging, Changyi mounted the wall and said: "The Son of Heaven ordered you, sir, to campaign against Cai Prefecture. Now you have come to Chen Prefecture; in righteousness I dare not admit you. Please quarter outside the city walls."
translations.idiomatic: Seeking lodging, Changyi mounted the wall and said: "The Son of Heaven ordered you, sir, to campaign against Cai Prefecture. Now you have come to Chen Prefecture; in righteousness I dare not admit you. Please quarter outside the city walls."

sentences.zh: 而從千騎入全義營，持牛酒勞軍。

translations.literal: Then, with a thousand horsemen, he entered Han Quanyi's camp and brought oxen and wine to treat the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Then, with a thousand horsemen, he entered Han Quanyi's camp and brought oxen and wine to treat the troops.

sentences.zh: 全義不自意，驚喜嘆服。

translations.literal: Quanyi had not expected it; he was astonished, sighed, and submitted in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi had not expected it. He was astonished, sighed, and submitted in admiration.

sentences.zh: 十八年，改充陳許行軍司馬。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, he was changed to serve as Mobile Headquarters Major of Chen and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was changed to serve as Mobile Headquarters Major of Chen and Xu.

sentences.zh: 明年，涚卒，詔昌裔為許州刺史，充陳許節度使，再加檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: The next year Qian died; an edict made Changyi Prefect of Xu Prefecture and Military Commissioner of Chen and Xu, and additionally made Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Qian died. An edict made Changyi Prefect of Xu Prefecture and Military Commissioner of Chen and Xu, and additionally made Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 元和八年五月，許州大水，壞廬舍，漂溺居人。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year of Yuanhe, great floods in Xu Prefecture destroyed dwellings and drowned inhabitants.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighth year of Yuanhe, great floods in Xu Prefecture destroyed dwellings and drowned inhabitants.

sentences.zh: 六月，征昌裔加檢校左僕射，兼左龍武統軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Changyi was summoned and additionally made Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrently Commander of the Left Dragon Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Changyi was summoned and additionally made Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrently Commander of the Left Dragon Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 初，昌裔以老疾而軍府無政，因其水敗軍府，上乃促令韓臯代之。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Changyi was aged and ill and the military government had no administration, and because the flood had ruined the military government, the emperor therefore urgently ordered Han Gao to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, because Changyi was aged and ill and the military government had no administration, and because the flood had ruined the military government, the emperor therefore urgently ordered Han Gao to replace him.

sentences.zh: 昌裔赴召，至長樂驛，聞有是命，乃上言風眩，請歸私第，許之。

translations.literal: Changyi answered the summons; when he reached Changle Relay Station and heard of this appointment, he submitted a memorial citing vertigo and asked to return to his private residence; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Changyi answered the summons. When he reached Changle Relay Station and heard of this appointment, he submitted a memorial citing vertigo and asked to return to his private residence, and this was granted.

sentences.zh: 其年卒，贈潞州大都督。

translations.literal: That year he died and was posthumously granted Grand Governor of Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died and was posthumously granted Grand Governor of Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 范希朝，字致君，河中虞鄉人。

translations.literal: Fan Xichao, courtesy name Zhijun, was a man of Yuxiang in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xichao, courtesy name Zhijun, was a man of Yuxiang in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 建中年，為邠寧虞候，戎政修舉，事節度使韓遊瑰。

translations.literal: In the Jianzhong years he was Chief Commandant of Bin and Ning, his military administration well ordered; he served the Military Commissioner Han Yougui.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianzhong years he was Chief Commandant of Bin and Ning, his military administration well ordered, and he served the Military Commissioner Han Yougui.

sentences.zh: 及德宗幸奉天，希朝戰守有功，累加兼中丞，為寧州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong reached Fengtian, Xichao had merit in fighting and holding the city; he was repeatedly promoted to additionally Vice Censor-in-Chief and Prefect of Ning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong reached Fengtian, Xichao had merit in fighting and holding the city. He was repeatedly promoted to additionally Vice Censor-in-Chief and Prefect of Ning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰入覲，自奉天歸邠州，以希朝素整肅有聲，畏其逼己，求其過，將殺之。

translations.literal: When Yougui entered court for an audience and returned to Bin Prefecture from Fengtian, because Xichao was by nature stern and had renown, he feared Xichao would press upon him, sought his faults, and was about to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yougui entered court for an audience and returned to Bin Prefecture from Fengtian, because Xichao was by nature stern and had renown, he feared Xichao would press upon him, sought his faults, and was about to kill him.

sentences.zh: 希朝懼，奔鳳翔。

translations.literal: Xichao was afraid and fled to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xichao was afraid and fled to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 德宗聞之，趣召至京師，置於左神策軍中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong heard of it, he urgently summoned Xichao to the capital and placed him in the Left Shence Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong heard of it, he urgently summoned Xichao to the capital and placed him in the Left Shence Army.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰歿，邠州諸將列名上請希朝為節度，德宗許之。

translations.literal: When Yougui died, the generals of Bin Prefecture listed their names and submitted a request that Xichao be made commissioner; Emperor Dezong granted it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yougui died, the generals of Bin Prefecture listed their names and submitted a request that Xichao be made commissioner, and Emperor Dezong granted it.

sentences.zh: 希朝讓於張獻甫，曰：「臣始逼而來，終代其任，非所以防凱覦安反側也。」

translations.literal: Xichao yielded the post to Zhang Xianfu, saying: "I came here at first because I was forced out, yet in the end I would replace him in his command — this is not the way to guard against covetous eyes and settle those inclined to rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: Xichao yielded the post to Zhang Xianfu, saying: "I came here at first because I was forced out, yet in the end I would replace him in his command — this is not the way to guard against covetous eyes and settle those inclined to rebellion."

sentences.zh: 詔嘉之，以獻甫統邠寧。

translations.literal: An edict praised this, and Xianfu was put in command of Bin and Ning.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised this, and Xianfu was put in command of Bin and Ning.

sentences.zh: 數日，除希朝振武節度使，就加檢校禮部尚書。

translations.literal: After several days, Xichao was made Military Commissioner of Zhenwu and thereupon additionally Acting Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After several days Xichao was made Military Commissioner of Zhenwu and thereupon additionally Acting Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 振武有党項、室韋，交居川阜，淩犯為盜，日入慝作，謂之「刮城門」。

translations.literal: At Zhenwu there were Tangut and Shiwei tribes intersecting in the valleys and hills; they raided as bandits, entering by stealth at dusk — an offense called "Peeling the City Gate."
translations.idiomatic: At Zhenwu the Tangut and Shiwei tribes intersected in the valleys and hills. They raided as bandits, entering by stealth at dusk in an offense called "Peeling the City Gate."

sentences.zh: 居人懼駭，鮮有寧日。

translations.literal: The inhabitants lived in fear and dread; rarely had they a day of peace.
translations.idiomatic: The inhabitants lived in fear and dread and rarely had a day of peace.

sentences.zh: 希朝周知要害，置堡柵，斥候嚴密，人遂獲安。

translations.literal: Xichao thoroughly knew the strategic points, set up fortresses and stockades, and made scouts and sentries strict; the people then obtained peace.
translations.idiomatic: Xichao thoroughly knew the strategic points, set up fortresses and stockades, and made scouts and sentries strict, and the people then obtained peace.

sentences.zh: 異蕃雖鼠竊狗盜，必殺無赦，戎虜甚憚之，曰：「有張光晟，苦我久矣，今聞是乃更姓名而來。」

translations.literal: Though the foreign tribes committed petty thefts, he invariably put them to death without mercy. The frontier tribes greatly feared him and said: "There was Zhang Guangcheng, who tormented us long; now we hear that this man has merely changed his name and come."
translations.idiomatic: Though the foreign tribes committed petty thefts, he invariably put them to death without mercy. The frontier tribes greatly feared him and said: "There was Zhang Guangcheng, who tormented us long; now we hear that this man has merely changed his name and come."

sentences.zh: 其見畏如此。

translations.literal: Such was the fear he inspired.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the fear he inspired.

sentences.zh: 蕃落之俗，有長帥至，必效奇駝名馬，雖廉者猶曰當從俗，以致其歡，希朝一無所受。

translations.literal: The custom of the tribal settlements was that when a new chief arrived, they would present rare camels and fine horses; even the incorruptible would say one must follow custom to win their favor — Xichao accepted nothing at all.
translations.idiomatic: The custom of the tribal settlements was that when a new chief arrived, they would present rare camels and fine horses. Even the incorruptible would say one must follow custom to win their favor — Xichao accepted nothing at all.

sentences.zh: 積十四年，皆保塞而不為橫。

translations.literal: Over fourteen years accumulated, all guarded the frontier and did not act violently.
translations.idiomatic: Over fourteen years accumulated, all guarded the frontier and did not act violently.

sentences.zh: 單于城中舊少樹，希朝於他處市柳子，命軍人種之，俄遂成林，居人賴之。

translations.literal: In the Single-Prince City there had long been few trees; Xichao bought willow seeds elsewhere and ordered the soldiers to plant them; soon they became a forest, and the inhabitants relied on them.
translations.idiomatic: In the Single-Prince City there had long been few trees. Xichao bought willow seeds elsewhere and ordered the soldiers to plant them. Soon they became a forest, and the inhabitants relied on them.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，累表請修朝覲。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenyuan era he repeatedly submitted memorials requesting to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenyuan era he repeatedly submitted memorials requesting to attend court.

sentences.zh: 時節將不以他故自述職者，惟希朝一人，德宗大悅。

translations.literal: At the time, of the frontier commanders who entered court for no other reason, Xichao alone did so; Emperor Dezong was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, of the frontier commanders who entered court for no other reason, Xichao alone did so, and Emperor Dezong was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 既至，拜檢校右僕射，兼右金吾大將軍。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he was appointed Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrently Grand General of the Right Jinwu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived he was appointed Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrently Grand General of the Right Jinwu Guard.

sentences.zh: 順宗時，王叔文黨用事，將授韓泰以兵柄；

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Shunzong, Wang Shuwen's faction held power and was about to grant Han Tai military authority;
translations.idiomatic: In the time of Emperor Shunzong, Wang Shuwen's faction held power and was about to grant Han Tai military authority;

sentences.zh: 利希朝老疾易制，乃命為左神策、京西諸城鎮行營節度使，鎮奉天，而以泰為副，欲因代之，叔文敗而罷。

translations.literal: They considered Xichao aged and ill and easy to control; they therefore appointed him Mobile Headquarters Commissioner of the Left Shence and the garrisons of the western capital region, garrisoning Fengtian, with Tai as deputy, intending to replace him thereby; when Shuwen fell, this was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: They considered Xichao aged and ill and easy to control. They therefore appointed him Mobile Headquarters Commissioner of the Left Shence and the garrisons of the western capital region, garrisoning Fengtian, with Tai as deputy, intending to replace him thereby. When Shuwen fell, this was abolished.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，復以檢校僕射為右金吾，出拜檢校司空，充朔方靈鹽節度使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong took the throne, he was again made Acting Vice Director as Right Jinwu Guard and went out as Acting Minister of Works and Military Commissioner of Shuofang and Ling and Salt.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong took the throne, he was again made Acting Vice Director as Right Jinwu Guard and went out as Acting Minister of Works and Military Commissioner of Shuofang and Ling and Salt.

sentences.zh: 突厥別部有沙陀者，北方推其勇勁，希朝誘致之，自甘州舉族來歸，眾且萬人。

translations.literal: Among the Turkic tribal divisions there were the Shatuo, whom the northern regions praised for courage and vigor; Xichao enticed them, and from Gan Prefecture the whole clan came to submit, numbering nearly ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Turkic tribal divisions there were the Shatuo, whom the northern regions praised for courage and vigor. Xichao enticed them, and from Gan Prefecture the whole clan came to submit, numbering nearly ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 其後以之討賊，所至有功，遷河東節度使。

translations.literal: Afterward they were used to campaign against rebels; wherever they went they had merit, and he was transferred to Military Commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward they were used to campaign against rebels. Wherever they went they had merit, and he was transferred to Military Commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 率師討鎮州無功。

translations.literal: He led troops to campaign against Zhen Prefecture without success.
translations.idiomatic: He led troops to campaign against Zhen Prefecture without success.

sentences.zh: 既耄且疾，事不理，除左龍武統軍，以太子太保致仕。

translations.literal: Already aged and ill, affairs went unmanaged; he was made Commander of the Left Dragon Martial Guard and retired as Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Already aged and ill, affairs went unmanaged. He was made Commander of the Left Dragon Martial Guard and retired as Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 元和九年卒，贈太子太師。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yuanhe he died and was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yuanhe he died and was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 希朝近代號為名將，人多比之趙充國。

translations.literal: In recent times Xichao was called a famous general; many compared him to Zhao Chongguo.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times Xichao was called a famous general; many compared him to Zhao Chongguo.

sentences.zh: 及張茂昭擊王承宗，幾覆，希朝玩寇不前，物議罪之。

translations.literal: When Zhang Maozhao attacked Wang Chengzong and nearly perished, Xichao dallied with the enemy and did not advance; public opinion blamed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Maozhao attacked Wang Chengzong and nearly perished, Xichao dallied with the enemy and did not advance, and public opinion blamed him.

sentences.zh: 王鍔，字昆吾，自言太原人。

translations.literal: Wang E, courtesy name Kunwu, said of himself that he was a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang E, courtesy name Kunwu, said of himself that he was a man of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 本湖南團練營將。

translations.literal: Originally a regimental officer of the Hunan Militia.
translations.idiomatic: Originally a regimental officer of the Hunan Militia.

sentences.zh: 初，楊炎貶道州司馬，鍔候炎於路，炎與言異之。

translations.literal: At first, when Yang Yan was demoted to Prefect of Daozhou, E waited for Yan on the road; Yan spoke with him and found him unusual.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Yang Yan was demoted to Prefect of Daozhou, E waited for Yan on the road. Yan spoke with him and found him unusual.

sentences.zh: 後嗣曹王臯為團練使，擢任鍔，頗便之。

translations.literal: Later, when Prince Cao Wang Gao succeeded as Militia Commissioner, he promoted and employed E and found him quite useful.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Prince Cao Wang Gao succeeded as Militia Commissioner, he promoted and employed E and found him quite useful.

sentences.zh: 使招邵州武岡叛將王國良有功，表為邵州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent to summon the rebel general Wang Guoliang of Wugang in Shao Prefecture and had merit; Gao memorialized him as Prefect of Shao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to summon the rebel general Wang Guoliang of Wugang in Shao Prefecture and had merit. Gao memorialized him as Prefect of Shao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及臯改江西節度使，李希烈南侵，臯請鍔以勁兵三千鎮尋陽。

translations.literal: When Gao was changed to Jiangxi Military Commissioner and Li Xilie invaded south, Gao requested E with three thousand crack troops to garrison Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao was changed to Jiangxi Military Commissioner and Li Xilie invaded south, Gao requested E with three thousand crack troops to garrison Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 後臯自以全軍臨九江，既襲得蘄州，盡以眾渡，乃表鍔為江州刺史、兼中丞，充都虞候，因以鍔從。

translations.literal: Later Gao himself brought the full army to Jiujiang; having taken Qizhou by surprise, he crossed with the entire force; he then memorialized E as Prefect of Jiang Prefecture, additionally Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Chief Commandant, and E followed Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Later Gao himself brought the full army to Jiujiang. Having taken Qizhou by surprise, he crossed with the entire force. He then memorialized E as Prefect of Jiang Prefecture, additionally Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Chief Commandant, and E followed Gao.

sentences.zh: 小心習事，善探得軍府情狀，至於言語動靜，巨細畢以白臯。

translations.literal: Careful and skilled in affairs, he was good at probing the military government's circumstances; as for speech and action, great and small, he reported all to Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Careful and skilled in affairs, he was good at probing the military government's circumstances. As for speech and action, great and small, he reported all to Gao.

sentences.zh: 臯亦推心委之，雖家宴妻女之會，鍔或在焉。

translations.literal: Gao also entrusted him wholeheartedly; even at family banquets with wife and daughters, E was sometimes present.
translations.idiomatic: Gao also entrusted him wholeheartedly. Even at family banquets with wife and daughters, E was sometimes present.

sentences.zh: 鍔感臯之知，事無所避。

translations.literal: E, moved by Gao's trust, shrank from nothing in his service.
translations.idiomatic: E, moved by Gao's trust, shrank from nothing in his service.

sentences.zh: 後臯攻安州，使伊慎盛兵圍之；

translations.literal: Later, when Gao attacked An Prefecture, he sent Yi Shen with a large force to besiege it;
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Gao attacked An Prefecture, he sent Yi Shen with a large force to besiege it;

sentences.zh: 賊懼，請臯使至城中以約降，臯使鍔懸而入。

translations.literal: The rebels were afraid and asked Gao to send an envoy into the city to arrange surrender; Gao sent E in alone by rope.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were afraid and asked Gao to send an envoy into the city to arrange surrender. Gao sent E in alone by rope.

sentences.zh: 既成約，殺不從者以出。

translations.literal: When the agreement was settled, he killed those who would not submit and came out.
translations.idiomatic: When the agreement was settled, he killed those who would not submit and came out.

sentences.zh: 明日城開，臯以其眾入。

translations.literal: The next day the city opened; Gao entered with his troops.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the city opened, and Gao entered with his troops.

sentences.zh: 伊慎以賊恟懼，由其圍也，不下鍔，鍔稱疾避之。

translations.literal: Yi Shen, because the rebels had been terrified by his siege, would not lower E; E claimed illness and avoided it.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Shen, because the rebels had been terrified by his siege, would not lower E. E claimed illness and avoided it.

sentences.zh: 及臯為荊南節度使，表鍔為江陵少尹、兼中丞，欲列於賓倅。

translations.literal: When Gao became Military Commissioner of Jingnan, he memorialized E as Vice Prefect of Jiangling, additionally Vice Censor-in-Chief, intending to rank him among the senior staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao became Military Commissioner of Jingnan, he memorialized E as Vice Prefect of Jiangling, additionally Vice Censor-in-Chief, intending to rank him among the senior staff.

sentences.zh: 馬彜、裴泰鄙鍔請去，乃復以為都虞候。

translations.literal: Ma Yi and Pei Tai despised E and asked to leave; he was then again made Chief Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yi and Pei Tai despised E and asked to leave. He was then again made Chief Commandant.

sentences.zh: 明年，從臯至京師，臯稱鍔於德宗曰：「鍔雖文用小不足，他皆可以試驗。」

translations.literal: The next year, following Gao to the capital, Gao praised E to Emperor Dezong, saying: "Though E is slightly lacking in literary and minor matters, in all else he may be tested."
translations.idiomatic: The next year, following Gao to the capital, Gao praised E to Emperor Dezong, saying: "Though E is slightly lacking in literary and minor matters, in all else he may be tested."

sentences.zh: 遂拜鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: Thereupon E was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon E was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 尋除容管經略使，凡八年，溪洞安之。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Commissioner for the Rongguan Frontier and, in all eight years, the stream valleys and caves were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Commissioner for the Rongguan Frontier and, in all eight years, the stream valleys and caves were pacified.

sentences.zh: 遷廣州刺史、御史大夫、嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Prefect of Guang Prefecture, Grand Censor, and Military Commissioner of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Prefect of Guang Prefecture, Grand Censor, and Military Commissioner of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 廣人與夷人雜處，地征薄而叢求於川市。

translations.literal: The people of Guang mixed with the tribal peoples; land levies were light but exactions clustered in the river markets.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Guang mixed with the tribal peoples. Land levies were light but exactions clustered in the river markets.

sentences.zh: 鍔能計居人之業而榷其利，所得與兩稅相埒。

translations.literal: E could calculate the occupations of residents and monopolize their profits; what he obtained matched the two tax levies.
translations.idiomatic: E could calculate the occupations of residents and monopolize their profits. What he obtained matched the two tax levies.

sentences.zh: 鍔以兩稅錢上供時進及供奉外，餘皆自入。

translations.literal: E used the two-tax funds for tribute to the court, seasonal presentations, and supplies beyond the regular quota; the remainder all entered his own purse.
translations.idiomatic: E used the two-tax funds for tribute to the court, seasonal presentations, and supplies beyond the regular quota. The remainder all entered his own purse.

sentences.zh: 西南大海中諸國舶至，則盡沒其利，由是鍔家財富於公藏。

translations.literal: Ships from the various kingdoms of the great southern sea arrived, and he seized all their profits; thereby E's household wealth exceeded the public treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Ships from the various kingdoms of the great southern sea arrived, and he seized all their profits. Thereby E's household wealth exceeded the public treasury.

sentences.zh: 日發十餘艇，重以犀象珠貝，稱商貸而出諸境。

translations.literal: Each day he dispatched more than ten boats, laden with rhinoceros horn, ivory, pearls, and shells, claiming them as merchant loans to send beyond the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he dispatched more than ten boats, laden with rhinoceros horn, ivory, pearls, and shells, claiming them as merchant loans to send beyond the borders.

sentences.zh: 周以歲時，循環不絕，凡八年，京師權門多富鍔之財。

translations.literal: Year by year the cycle never ceased; in all eight years, many powerful families at the capital grew rich on E's wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Year by year the cycle never ceased. In all eight years many powerful families at the capital grew rich on E's wealth.

sentences.zh: 拜刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 時淮南節度使杜佑屢請代，乃以鍔檢校兵部尚書，充淮南副節度使。

translations.literal: At the time the Huainan Military Commissioner Du You repeatedly requested replacement; E was then made Acting Minister of War and Deputy Military Commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Huainan Military Commissioner Du You repeatedly requested replacement. E was then made Acting Minister of War and Deputy Military Commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 鍔始見佑，以趨拜悅佑，退坐司馬廳事。

translations.literal: When E first met You, he pleased You with hurried bows; afterward he sat in the major's hall.
translations.idiomatic: When E first met You, he pleased You with hurried bows. Afterward he sat in the major's hall.

sentences.zh: 數日，詔杜佑以鍔代之。

translations.literal: After several days, an edict made Du You replaced by E.
translations.idiomatic: After several days, an edict made Du You replaced by E.

sentences.zh: 鍔明習簿領，善小數以持下，吏或有奸，鍔畢究之。

translations.literal: E was skilled in ledgers and registers and good at small calculations in controlling subordinates; if any clerk was corrupt, E thoroughly investigated him.
translations.idiomatic: E was skilled in ledgers and registers and good at small calculations in controlling subordinates. If any clerk was corrupt, E thoroughly investigated him.

sentences.zh: 嘗聽理，有遺匿名書於前者，左右取以授鍔，鍔內之靴中，靴中先有他書以雜之。

translations.literal: Once while hearing cases, an anonymous letter was left in front; attendants took it and handed it to E; E put it inside his boot, and inside the boot there was already another letter to mix with it.
translations.idiomatic: Once while hearing cases, an anonymous letter was left in front. Attendants took it and handed it to E. E put it inside his boot, and inside the boot there was already another letter to mix with it.

sentences.zh: 及吏退，鍔探取他書焚之，人信其以所匿名者焚也。

translations.literal: When the clerks withdrew, E drew out the other letter and burned it; people believed he had burned the anonymous one.
translations.idiomatic: When the clerks withdrew, E drew out the other letter and burned it. People believed he had burned the anonymous one.

sentences.zh: 既歸省所告者，異日乃以他微事連其所告者，固窮按驗之以譎眾，下吏以為神明。

translations.literal: Returning to his quarters he examined the accuser; another day he linked some other minor matter to the accused, firmly pressed and verified it by stratagem to deceive the crowd, and subordinates thought him divine.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to his quarters he examined the accuser. Another day he linked some other minor matter to the accused, firmly pressed and verified it by stratagem to deceive the crowd, and subordinates thought him divine.

sentences.zh: 鍔長於部領，程作有法，軍州所用竹木，其餘碎屑無所棄，皆復為用。

translations.literal: E excelled at commanding troops; construction followed method, and bamboo and wood used by the army and prefectures — even the leftover scraps — were not discarded but all put to use again.
translations.idiomatic: E excelled at commanding troops. Construction followed method, and bamboo and wood used by the army and prefectures—even the leftover scraps—were not discarded but all put to use again.

sentences.zh: 掾曹簾壞，吏以新簾易之，鍔察知，以故者付舡坊以替箬，其他率如此。

translations.literal: When a clerk's curtain was ruined, the clerk replaced it with a new one; E detected this and gave the old one to the boat yard to replace matting — the rest was mostly thus.
translations.idiomatic: When a clerk's curtain was ruined, the clerk replaced it with a new one. E detected this and gave the old one to the boat yard to replace matting—the rest was mostly thus.

sentences.zh: 每有饗宴，輒錄其餘以備後用，或云賣之，收利皆自歸，故鍔錢流衍天下。

translations.literal: Whenever there was a feast, he recorded the leftovers to prepare for later use, or it was said he sold them; the profit all went to himself — thus E's money circulated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever there was a feast he recorded the leftovers to prepare for later use, or it was said he sold them. The profit all went to himself, and thus E's money circulated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 在鎮四年，累至司空。

translations.literal: After four years in command he was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After four years in command he was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 元和二年來朝，真拜左僕射，未幾除檢校司徒、河中節度。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhe he came to court and was appointed in full as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; before long he was made Acting Grand Preceptor and Military Commissioner of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanhe he came to court and was appointed in full as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs. Before long he was made Acting Grand Preceptor and Military Commissioner of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 居三年，兼太子太傅，移鎮太原。

translations.literal: After three years he was additionally Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent and transferred to garrison Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he was additionally Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent and transferred to garrison Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 時方討鎮州，鍔緝綏訓練，軍府稱理。
