translations.literal: At the time they were campaigning against Zhen Prefecture; E restored order, trained troops, and the military government was praised as well governed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time they were campaigning against Zhen Prefecture. E restored order, trained troops, and the military government was praised as well governed.

sentences.zh: 鍔受符節居方面凡二十餘年。

translations.literal: E held the seal and staff in a frontier command for more than twenty years in all.
translations.idiomatic: E held the seal and staff in a frontier command for more than twenty years in all.

sentences.zh: 九年，加同平章事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was additionally Co-equal with the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was additionally Co-equal with the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十年卒，年七十六，贈太尉。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died, age seventy-six; he was posthumously granted Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he died at the age of seventy-six and was posthumously granted Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 鍔將卒，約束後事甚明，如知其死日。

translations.literal: When E was about to die, he arranged his later affairs with great clarity, as though he knew the day of his death.
translations.idiomatic: When E was about to die, he arranged his later affairs with great clarity, as though he knew the day of his death.

sentences.zh: 鍔附太原王翃為從子，以婚閥自炫，炫子弟多附鍔以致名宦。

translations.literal: E attached himself to Wang Hong of Taiyuan as a nephew and flaunted marriage alliances; Hong's younger kinsmen mostly attached themselves to E to obtain fame and office.
translations.idiomatic: E attached himself to Wang Hong of Taiyuan as a nephew and flaunted marriage alliances. Hong's younger kinsmen mostly attached themselves to E to obtain fame and office.

sentences.zh: 又嘗讀《春秋左氏傳》，自稱儒者，人皆笑之。

translations.literal: He also once read the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals and called himself a Confucian; people all laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: He also once read the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals and called himself a Confucian. People all laughed at him.

sentences.zh: 子稷，歷官鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: His son Ji held the post of Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji held the post of Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 鍔在籓鎮，稷嘗留京師，以家財奉權要，視官高下以進賂，不待白其父而行之。

translations.literal: When E was in a frontier command, Ji was left at the capital; he used the family wealth to serve the powerful, advancing bribes according to the rank of office without informing his father.
translations.idiomatic: When E was in a frontier command, Ji was left at the capital. He used the family wealth to serve the powerful, advancing bribes according to the rank of office without informing his father.

sentences.zh: 廣治第宅，嘗奏請藉坊以益之，作復垣洞穴，實金錢於其中。

translations.literal: He extensively built mansions and once memorialized requesting the Jie Fang ward to expand them, constructing compound walls and hidden chambers and storing gold and money within.
translations.idiomatic: He extensively built mansions and once memorialized requesting the Jie Fang ward to expand them, constructing compound walls and hidden chambers and storing gold and money within.

sentences.zh: 貴官清品，溺其賞宴而遊，不憚清議。

translations.literal: Noble officials and pure-rank gentlemen, drowned in his lavish feasts, came and went without fear of censure.
translations.idiomatic: Noble officials and pure-rank gentlemen, drowned in his lavish feasts, came and went without fear of censure.

sentences.zh: 及父卒，為奴所告稷換鍔遺表，隱沒所進錢物。

translations.literal: When his father died, a slave reported that Ji had altered E's deathbed memorial and concealed the money and goods he had presented.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, a slave reported that Ji had altered E's deathbed memorial and concealed the money and goods he had presented.

sentences.zh: 上令鞫其奴於內仗，又發中使就東都驗責其家財。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the slave interrogated in the inner guard office and also sent a court envoy to the eastern capital to verify and exact his household wealth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the slave interrogated in the inner guard office and also sent a court envoy to the eastern capital to verify and exact his household wealth.

sentences.zh: 宰臣裴度苦諫，於是罷其使而殺奴。

translations.literal: Grand Councillor Pei Du remonstrated bitterly; the envoy was then recalled and the slave killed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councillor Pei Du remonstrated bitterly. The envoy was then recalled and the slave killed.

sentences.zh: 稷長慶二年為德州刺史，廣賫金寶仆妾以行。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changqing, Ji was Prefect of De Prefecture; he brought abundant gold, jewels, concubines, and servants on his journey.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changqing Ji was Prefect of De Prefecture. He brought abundant gold, jewels, concubines, and servants on his journey.

sentences.zh: 節度使李全略利其貨而圖之，故致本州軍亂，殺稷，其室女為全略所虜，以妓媵處之。

translations.literal: The Military Commissioner Li Quanlue coveted his goods and plotted against him; he therefore incited rebellion in the prefectural army, killed Ji, and his daughter was taken by Quanlue and kept as a singing-girl concubine.
translations.idiomatic: The Military Commissioner Li Quanlue coveted his goods and plotted against him. He therefore incited rebellion in the prefectural army, killed Ji, and his daughter was taken by Quanlue and kept as a singing-girl concubine.

sentences.zh: 稷子叔泰。

translations.literal: Ji's son Shutai.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's son Shutai.

sentences.zh: 開成四年，滄州節度使劉約上言：「王稷為李全略所殺，家無遺類。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaicheng, the Cang Prefecture Military Commissioner Liu Yue submitted a memorial saying: "Wang Ji was killed by Li Quanlue, and his household left no survivors.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaicheng, the Cang Prefecture Military Commissioner Liu Yue submitted a memorial saying: "Wang Ji was killed by Li Quanlue, and his household left no survivors.

sentences.zh: 稷男叔泰，時年五歲，郡人宋忠獻匿之獲免，乃收養之，今已成長。

translations.literal: Ji's son Shutai was then five years old; the county man Song Zhongxian hid him and he escaped; he was then reared, and now he has grown to maturity.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's son Shutai was then five years old. The county man Song Zhongxian hid him and he escaped, was then reared, and now he has grown to maturity.

sentences.zh: 臣獎其義，忠獻已補職，叔泰津送以聞。」

translations.literal: Your subject rewards this righteousness; Zhongxian has already been given an appointment, and Shutai is sent by river transport to report."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject rewards this righteousness. Zhongxian has already been given an appointment, and Shutai is sent by river transport to report."

sentences.zh: 文宗詔曰：「王鍔累朝宣力，王稷一旦捐軀，須錄孤遺，微申憫念。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong issued an edict saying: "Wang E exerted himself across successive reigns; Wang Ji perished in a single day; we must record the orphaned survivor and slightly express our compassionate remembrance.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong issued an edict saying: "Wang E exerted himself across successive reigns; Wang Ji perished in a single day; we must record the orphaned survivor and slightly express our compassionate remembrance.

sentences.zh: 王叔泰委吏部與九品官，令奉祭。」

translations.literal: Wang Shutai is entrusted to the Ministry of Personnel for a ninth-rank office, with orders to perform the sacrifices."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shutai is entrusted to the Ministry of Personnel for a ninth-rank office, with orders to perform the sacrifices."

sentences.zh: 閻巨源，貞元十九年以勝州刺史攝振武行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Yan Juyuan, in the nineteenth year of Zhenyuan, as Prefect of Sheng Prefecture acted as Mobile Headquarters Major of Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Juyuan, in the nineteenth year of Zhenyuan, as Prefect of Sheng Prefecture acted as Mobile Headquarters Major of Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 屬希朝入覲，遂代為節度。

translations.literal: When Xichao entered court for an audience, he then replaced him as commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Xichao entered court for an audience, he then replaced him as commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以材力進，無他智能。

translations.literal: He advanced by strength and ability; he had no other talent or wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced by strength and ability and had no other talent or wisdom.

sentences.zh: 初不知書而好文，其言輒乖誤，時人多摭其談說以為戲，然以寬厚為將卒所懷。

translations.literal: At first he did not know writing yet loved literature; his words were always mistaken, and people often collected his remarks for amusement — yet as a general he was trusted by the troops for his leniency and generosity.
translations.idiomatic: At first he did not know writing yet loved literature. His words were always mistaken, and people often collected his remarks for amusement — yet as a general he was trusted by the troops for his leniency and generosity.

sentences.zh: 後為邠寧節度使、檢校左僕射。

translations.literal: Later he was Military Commissioner of Bin and Ning and Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Military Commissioner of Bin and Ning and Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 元和九年卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yuanhe he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yuanhe he died.

sentences.zh: 孟元陽，起於陳許軍中，理戎整肅，勤事，善部署。

translations.literal: Meng Yuanyang rose from the Chen and Xu army; he ordered troops sternly, served diligently, and was skilled in deployment.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Yuanyang rose from the Chen and Xu army. He ordered troops sternly, served diligently, and was skilled in deployment.

sentences.zh: 曲環之為節度，元陽已為大將，環使董作西華屯。

translations.literal: When Qu Huan became commissioner, Yuanyang was already a great general; Huan had him oversee construction at Xihua Colony.
translations.idiomatic: When Qu Huan became commissioner, Yuanyang was already a great general. Huan had him oversee construction at Xihua Colony.

sentences.zh: 元陽盛夏芒戺立稻田中，須役者退而後就舍，故其田歲無不稔，軍中足食。

translations.literal: Yuanyang in midsummer stood in the rice fields in grass-cloth, waiting until the laborers withdrew before going to quarters; thus his fields every year were never without a full harvest, and the army had ample food.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyang in midsummer stood in the rice fields in grass-cloth, waiting until the laborers withdrew before going to quarters. Thus his fields every year were never without a full harvest, and the army had ample food.

sentences.zh: 環卒，吳少誠寇許州，元陽城守；

translations.literal: When Huan died, Wu Shaocheng raided Xu Prefecture; Yuanyang held the city;
translations.idiomatic: When Huan died, Wu Shaocheng raided Xu Prefecture. Yuanyang held the city;

sentences.zh: 外無救兵，攻圍甚急，而終不能傅其城，賊乃罷兵。

translations.literal: Outside there were no relief troops; the siege was very pressing, yet in the end they could not reach the wall; the rebels then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Outside there were no relief troops and the siege was very pressing, yet in the end they could not reach the wall. The rebels then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 韓全義五樓之敗，諸軍多私歸，元陽及神策都將蘇元策、宣州都將王幹各率部留軍溵水，破賊二千餘人。

translations.literal: When Han Quanyi was defeated at the Five Towers, many armies privately returned; Yuanyang and the Shence Chief General Su Yuance, and the Xuan Prefecture Chief General Wang Gan, each led their divisions and remained at Wen River, breaking more than two thousand rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Quanyi was defeated at the Five Towers, many armies privately returned. Yuanyang and the Shence Chief General Su Yuance, and the Xuan Prefecture Chief General Wang Gan, each led their divisions and remained at Wen River, breaking more than two thousand rebels.

sentences.zh: 兵罷，加御史大夫。

translations.literal: When the campaign ended, he was additionally made Grand Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign ended he was additionally made Grand Censor.

sentences.zh: 元和初，拜河陽節度、檢校尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was appointed Military Commissioner of Heyang and Acting Minister.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was appointed Military Commissioner of Heyang and Acting Minister.

sentences.zh: 五年，拜右僕射、昭義節度，入為右羽林統軍，封趙國公。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Military Commissioner of Zhaoyi, entered court as Commander of the Right Feathered Forest Guard, and enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Military Commissioner of Zhaoyi, entered court as Commander of the Right Feathered Forest Guard, and enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 俄拜左金吾大將軍，復除統軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand General of the Left Jinwu Guard and again made Commander of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Grand General of the Left Jinwu Guard and again made Commander of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 元和九年卒，贈揚州大都督。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yuanhe he died and was posthumously granted Grand Governor of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yuanhe he died and was posthumously granted Grand Governor of Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 趙昌，字洪祚，天水人。

translations.literal: Zhao Chang, courtesy name Hongzuo, was a man of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chang, courtesy name Hongzuo, was a man of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 祖不器，父居貞，皆有名於時。

translations.literal: His grandfather Buqi and father Juzhen were both renowned in their time.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Buqi and father Juzhen were both renowned in their time.

sentences.zh: 李承昭為昭義節度，辟昌在幕府。

translations.literal: When Li Chengzhao was Military Commissioner of Zhaoyi, he recruited Chang to his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Chengzhao was Military Commissioner of Zhaoyi, he recruited Chang to his staff.

sentences.zh: 貞元七年，為虔州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenyuan he was Prefect of Qian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhenyuan he was Prefect of Qian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 屬安南都護為夷獠所逐，拜安南都護，夷人率化。

translations.literal: When the Protector-General of Annan was driven out by tribal raiders, Chang was appointed Protector-General and the tribes submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Protector-General of Annan was driven out by tribal raiders, Chang was appointed Protector-General and the tribes submitted.

sentences.zh: 十年，因屋壞傷脛，懇疏乞還，以檢校兵部郎中裴泰代之，入拜國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, when a building collapse injured his shin, he earnestly memorialized asking to return; Pei Tai was appointed Acting Director in the Ministry of War to replace him, and Chang entered court as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, when a building collapse injured his shin, he earnestly memorialized asking to return. Pei Tai was appointed Acting Director in the Ministry of War to replace him, and Chang entered court as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 及泰為首領所逐，德宗詔昌問狀。

translations.literal: When Tai was driven out by the chieftains, Emperor Dezong ordered Chang to inquire into the situation.
translations.idiomatic: When Tai was driven out by the chieftains, Emperor Dezong ordered Chang to inquire into the situation.

sentences.zh: 昌時年七十二，而精健如少年者，德宗奇之，復命為都護，南人相賀。

translations.literal: Chang was then seventy-two years old yet vigorous as a youth; Emperor Dezong marveled at this and again appointed him Protector-General; the southern people congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was then seventy-two years old yet vigorous as a youth. Emperor Dezong marveled at this and again appointed him Protector-General, and the southern people congratulated one another.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，加檢校工部尚書，尋轉戶部尚書，充嶺南節度。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong took the throne, he was additionally made Acting Minister of Works; soon he was transferred to Minister of Revenue and made Military Commissioner of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong took the throne, he was additionally made Acting Minister of Works. Soon he was transferred to Minister of Revenue and made Military Commissioner of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 元和三年，遷鎮荊南，徵為太子賓客。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanhe he was transferred to garrison Jingnan and summoned as Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanhe he was transferred to garrison Jingnan and summoned as Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 及得見，拜工部尚書、兼大理卿。

translations.literal: When he was received in audience, he was appointed Minister of Works and concurrently Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When he was received in audience he was appointed Minister of Works and concurrently Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，讓卿守本官。

translations.literal: After more than a year he yielded the judgeship and kept his original office.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he yielded the judgeship and kept his original office.

sentences.zh: 六年，除華州刺史，辭於麟德殿。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was made Prefect of Hua Prefecture and took leave at Linde Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made Prefect of Hua Prefecture and took leave at Linde Hall.

sentences.zh: 時年八十餘，趨拜輕捷，召對詳明，上退而嘆異，宣宰臣密訪其頤養之道以奏焉。

translations.literal: He was then more than eighty years old; his hurried bows were light and agile, and his responses in audience were detailed and clear; when the emperor withdrew he sighed in wonder and ordered the councillors secretly to inquire into his methods of nourishing life and memorialize them.
translations.idiomatic: He was then more than eighty years old. His hurried bows were light and agile, and his responses in audience were detailed and clear. When the emperor withdrew he sighed in wonder and ordered the councillors secretly to inquire into his methods of nourishing life and memorialize them.

sentences.zh: 在郡三年，入為太子少保。

translations.literal: After three years in the commandery he entered court as Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in the commandery he entered court as Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 九年卒，年八十五，贈揚州大都督，謚曰成。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died, age eighty-five; he was posthumously granted Grand Governor of Yang Prefecture and given the posthumous title Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he died at the age of eighty-five. He was posthumously granted Grand Governor of Yang Prefecture and given the posthumous title Cheng.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：高崇文以律貞師，勤於軍政，戎麾指蜀，遽立奇功，可謂近朝之良將也。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Gao Congwen disciplined the army with law and integrity, was diligent in military administration, pointed his banner toward Shu, and swiftly established extraordinary merit — he may be called a fine general of recent times.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Gao Congwen disciplined the army with law and integrity, was diligent in military administration, pointed his banner toward Shu, and swiftly established extraordinary merit — he may be called a fine general of recent times.

sentences.zh: 伊慎、朱忠亮、劉昌裔、范希朝、閻巨源、孟元陽、趙昌等，各立功立事，亦一時之名臣。

translations.literal: Yi Shen, Zhu Zhongliang, Liu Changyi, Fan Xichao, Yan Juyuan, Meng Yuanyang, Zhao Chang, and the rest each established merit and affairs and were also famous ministers of their time.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Shen, Zhu Zhongliang, Liu Changyi, Fan Xichao, Yan Juyuan, Meng Yuanyang, Zhao Chang, and the rest each established merit and affairs and were also famous ministers of their time.

sentences.zh: 王鍔明可照奸，忠能奉主，此乃垂名於後也。

translations.literal: Wang E's clarity could expose treachery, and his loyalty could serve his lord — this is what leaves a name for posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Wang E's clarity could expose treachery, and his loyalty could serve his lord — this is what leaves a name for posterity.

sentences.zh: 至若竹頭木屑，曾無棄遺，作事有程，儉而足用，則又士君子之為也。

translations.literal: As for bamboo scraps and wood shavings, never discarded; affairs conducted with measure; thrift yet sufficient for use — this again is the conduct of a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: As for bamboo scraps and wood shavings never discarded, affairs conducted with measure, thrift yet sufficient for use — this again is the conduct of a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 如賤收貴出，務積珠金，唯利是求，多財為累，則與夫清白遺子孫者遠矣！

translations.literal: But to buy cheap and sell dear, to strive to amass pearls and gold, to seek profit alone and be burdened by great wealth — this is far from leaving one's descendants an inheritance of integrity!
translations.idiomatic: But to buy cheap and sell dear, to strive to amass pearls and gold, to seek profit alone and be burdened by great wealth — this is far from leaving one's descendants an inheritance of integrity!

sentences.zh: 凡百在位，得不鑒之。

translations.literal: All who hold office — can they not take this as a mirror?
translations.idiomatic: All who hold office — can they not take this as a mirror?

sentences.zh: 贊曰：崇文之功，顯於西蜀。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Congwen's merit was displayed in western Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy says: Congwen's merit was displayed in western Shu.

sentences.zh: 伊慎之忠，見乎南服。

translations.literal: Yi Shen's loyalty appeared in the southern domains.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Shen's loyalty appeared in the southern domains.

sentences.zh: 朱、劉、范、閻，各有其目。

translations.literal: Zhu, Liu, Fan, and Yan each had his own measure.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu, Liu, Fan, and Yan each had his own measure.

sentences.zh: 元陽、趙昌，不無遺躅。

translations.literal: Yuanyang and Zhao Chang were not without traces left behind.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyang and Zhao Chang were not without traces left behind.

sentences.zh: 惟彼太原，戰勛可錄。

translations.literal: As for that man of Taiyuan, his battle merit may be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: As for that man of Taiyuan, his battle merit may be recorded.

sentences.zh: 累在多財，子孫不祿。

translations.literal: Burdened by great wealth, his descendants did not enjoy emolument.
translations.idiomatic: Burdened by great wealth, his descendants did not enjoy emolument.
